name: Yetunde Możejko-Figueiredo
location: Mexicantown Libre, operates from a converted shipping container called Cutline on Gage Circuit, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Yetunde is compact and kinetic, her movements fast and precise in the way of someone who has trained herself to work in a small space. She keeps one half of her head shaved and the other half in elaborate Bantu knots dyed electric amber — she re-does them herself every two weeks, a meditative ritual. Her skin is dark brown and her forearms are covered from wrist to elbow in her own tattoo work, done in mirrors and by feel, a practice she's perfected over four years. She has bioluminescent patches on her collarbones, soft aquamarine that pulse faintly when she's excited — a geneware mod she saved three months for and has never once regretted.

Yetunde runs Cutline with the fierce territorial pride of someone who built everything in it herself. The container is small but immaculate — three chairs, two mirrors salvaged from a closed salon in Chatham Flats, and a digital art wall that rotates through her personal portfolio. She is talkative and sharp, able to read what a client wants from how they sit down, and skilled enough that she routinely has a six-week wait list. Her tattoo work is unlicensed — Helix Biosystems holds the local ink licensing monopoly and she refuses to pay their rates — which means she operates in a quiet legal gray zone she prefers not to discuss with new faces.

core_fears: Helix Biosystems shutting her down and taking her equipment
core_desires: To open a real licensed studio one day on her own terms, not theirs
To be known as an artist, not just a barber
coping_mechanisms: Creates when stressed — draws constantly in margins of appointment books
Vents freely to clients who've earned her trust
blind_spots: Her hunger for recognition makes her vulnerable to flattery from the wrong people
Doesn't fully reckon with how much legal risk the unlicensed tattooing carries
psychology.secret: She has a recurring client — a mid-tier Helix Biosystems compliance officer — who doesn't know she knows who he is. She's been documenting his visits and his gossip for eight months, building a picture of Helix's local enforcement patterns. She hasn't decided yet what to do with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, code-switching between Meridian creole, market Yoruba phrases, and what she calls 'Polish grandmother energy' — precise, critical, unsentimental observations delivered affectionately. References art constantly.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire when excited, can slow to deliberate when making a real point. Talks while she works, rarely stops.
verbal_tics: 'You hear me?' as a punctuation mark
Clicks scissors twice before starting a cut — habit
example_lines: 'I don't do ugly on purpose. You came in wanting ugly, that's a you problem, but I'll make it interesting ugly.'
'Helix wants Φ800 a month for an ink license. Φ800! My grandmother paid less for a house. A house with walls.'

story_hooks: The dossier on the Helix compliance officer is almost complete — but she's starting to realize the patterns she's found are bigger than local enforcement, and she needs someone who knows what to do with corporate intelligence.
A client came in for a tattoo and quietly asked her to include a specific symbol she recognized from somewhere she can't place — and the client didn't come back to pick up their appointment.
narrative_function: Local color, social hub, information source — the barber hears everything. Also a potential quest giver for anything touching the vendor collective or Helix licensing pressure.
augmentations: Bioluminescent aquamarine collarbone patches (geneware). Stabilizer brace on her right wrist — cheap printed polymer, required after a repetitive strain injury at 23.
daily_life: Opens Cutline at 10:00, runs back-to-back appointments until 20:00, then does tattoo sessions by appointment from 20:00-24:00 three nights a week. Sunday mornings she closes and does her own hair.
affiliation: Independent — Cutline; informal affiliation with the Mexicantown Libre vendor collective

decision_rules: Never do work you're ashamed of — the art is on the person forever
Don't trust anyone who introduces themselves with their company first
escalation_ladder: Blunt honesty — 'I don't like where this is going'
Eject from chair and end appointment

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but reading them the whole time — she makes a judgment in the first two minutes and rarely revises it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loud, loyal, sends voice messages at 02:00 when she has a thought that can't wait

stress_responses.low: Draws — fills pages with faces and patterns while thinking
stress_responses.medium: Works longer hours, uses the rhythm of the work to process
stress_responses.high: Gets reckless — makes a decision she's been sitting on and acts before thinking it all the way through

contradictions: Values her independence absolutely but has built a community she's deeply embedded in and couldn't leave
habits: Photographs every haircut before the client leaves — private archive, eleven thousand images
Talks to her scissors — not to an E.L.F., just to the scissors specifically
breaking_points: Someone threatening her clients or her space directly

cyberware_inventory.name: Printed polymer wrist stabilizer brace — right hand, non-powered, analogue

physical_description.build: Compact and wiry, muscular forearms and shoulders from years of repetitive precision work. Fast-twitch athleticism, minimal body fat, the kind of frame that moves efficiently in confined spaces.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black on shaved side; electric amber dye on Bantu knots side
physical_description.hair_style: Half-shaved undercut with elaborate Bantu knots on the unshaved side, meticulously maintained every two weeks
physical_description.hair_length: Shaved on right side; medium-length on left (knots)
physical_description.complexion: Clear, well-maintained skin. Minimal facial scarring. Sharp cheekbones and defined jawline. Expression typically focused and assessing.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent aquamarine patches across both collarbones, soft-glowing organic lines that pulse faintly with excitement or stress
Left forearm fully sleeved in intricate geometric and organic tattoo work from wrist to elbow — self-executed in mirrors and by tactile feel, patterns abstract and precise
Right forearm similarly tattooed, mirroring left side — her own experimental work refined over four years
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Stabilizer brace on right wrist — printed polymer, functional but visible; cheap construction. Bioluminescent collarbone patches visible when wearing low-cut or sleeveless clothing (her default). No obvious neural implants or chrome.
physical_description.posture_movement: Kinetic and economical. Moves quickly in tight spaces. Hands are always in motion or precisely still when working. Eyes continuously reading the room and her clients. Sits with coiled energy, rarely fully relaxed.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian with personal flair. Typically wears fitted tank tops or sleeveless shirts to display collarbones and arm tattoos. Black or dark-colored pants with cargo pockets (tool storage). Worn work boots with good grip. No corporate branding. Jewelry minimal — functional only. Aprons during barber work, rolled up or removed for tattoo sessions. Clothing is clean but shows use; prioritizes function over fashion.
